The document is a technical E2E test spec about reproducing a production failure (missing id on a ## heading) and ensuring crash-safe slug derivation. Neither mapped area substantively covers E2E testing, slug generation, memory pipeline phases, or crash prevention — the graph has no areas for engineering/testing practice, ID derivation, or pipeline behavior. I expanded both available strategy decisions because DiagnosticFirst's emphasis on understanding systems before proposing solutions is the closest thematic neighbor to a document about reproducing and diagnosing a production failure pattern, and KnowledgeMapping's focus on visualizing where knowledge lives could marginally bear on the memory-pipeline context. No other areas exist in this perspective to expand.

Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). positions.frame: what must this test case guarantee, given the missing-id failure pattern it reproduces?
positions.why: src-1 grounds the test in a concrete, production-observed defect (expert framing, calm-negative register — a known failure stated flatly, not alarmed over) while src-2 states the acceptance criterion that closes the loop on that defect (calm-positive, matter-of-fact, authority-ranking directive delivered as a settled rule via paired 'must' clauses). Read together they form one unit: the reproduction target and the passing condition for the same derive-id slug-generation test. The tension is between the negative-toned diagnosis (a defect exists) and the confident, almost pre-settled tone of the requirement (the fix is simply what must hold) — both readable as facets of a single test-case definition, not competing claims.
